evidence.title: Minoru Inuzuka
evidence.text: Minoru Inuzuka (犬塚 稔 , Inuzuka Minoru , 15 February 1901 – 17 September 2007) was a Japanese film director and screenwriter.

evidence.title: Minoru Inuzuka
evidence.text: Starting out as a screenwriter at Shochiku in 1924, he also participated in the production of Teinosuke Kinugasa's "A Page of Madness".

evidence.title: Minoru Inuzuka
evidence.text: When Chōjirō Hayashi (later known as Kazuo Hasegawa) became a jidaigeki star at Shochiku, Inuzuka directed many of his films.

evidence.title: Minoru Inuzuka
evidence.text: After World War II, Inuzuka returned to specializing in screenplays and was known for his scripts for the Zatoichi series.

evidence.title: Minoru Inuzuka
evidence.text: He published his autobiography in 2002, and died in 2007 at the age of 106.

evidence.title: Minoru Inuzuka
evidence.text: When he died, he was called the last surviving director to have directed a silent film in the 1920s.

evidence.title: Minoru Inuzuka
evidence.text: Inuzuka wrote scripts for over 150 films and directed over 50.

evidence.title: Dedication of the Great Buddha
evidence.text: Dedication of the Great Buddha (大仏開眼 , Daibutsu kaigen ) is a 1952 Japanese film directed by Teinosuke Kinugasa.

evidence.title: Dedication of the Great Buddha
evidence.text: It was entered into the 1953 Cannes Film Festival.

evidence.title: Teinosuke Kinugasa
evidence.text: Teinosuke Kinugasa (衣笠 貞之助 , Kinugasa Teinosuke ) (1 January 1896 – 26 February 1982) was a Japanese actor and film director.

evidence.title: Teinosuke Kinugasa
evidence.text: He was born in Kameyama, Mie Prefecture and died in Kyoto.

evidence.title: Teinosuke Kinugasa
evidence.text: Kinugasa won the 1954 Palme d'or at Cannes for "Jigokumon" ("The Gate of Hell").

evidence.title: The Romance of Yushima
evidence.text: The Romance of Yushima (婦系図 湯島の白梅 , Onna Keizu Yushima no Shiraume ) (おんなけいず ゆしまのしらうめ), aka "The White Plum of Yushima", is a 1955 black-and-white Japanese film directed by Teinosuke Kinugasa.

evidence.title: Don O. Newland
evidence.text: Don Oliver Newland (1896–1951) was an American film director and producer whose career consisted largely of itinerant work.

evidence.title: Don O. Newland
evidence.text: From the 1920s until his death, he traveled to cities throughout the United States making films that employed local citizens as stars and extras.

evidence.title: Don O. Newland
evidence.text: Using a standard script, Newland personalized each film according to its location – "Belvidere's Hero", "Staunton's Hero", "Janesville's Hero", "Huntingdon's Hero", "Tyrone's Hero", "Wilmington's Hero", and so on.

evidence.title: A Page of Madness
evidence.text: A Page of Madness (狂った一頁 , Kurutta Ippēji or Kurutta Ichipeiji ) is a silent film by Japanese film director Teinosuke Kinugasa, made in 1926.

evidence.title: A Page of Madness
evidence.text: It was lost for forty-five years until being rediscovered by Kinugasa in his storehouse in 1971.

evidence.title: A Page of Madness
evidence.text: The film is the product of an avant-garde group of artists in Japan known as the Shinkankakuha (or School of New Perceptions) who tried to overcome naturalistic representation.

evidence.title: 1954 Cannes Film Festival
evidence.text: The 7th Cannes Film Festival was held from 25 March to 9 April 1954.

evidence.title: 1954 Cannes Film Festival
evidence.text: With Jean Cocteau as President of the Jury, the Grand Prix went to the "Gate of Hell" by Teinosuke Kinugasa.

evidence.title: 1954 Cannes Film Festival
evidence.text: The festival opened with "Le Grand Jeu" by Robert Siodmak.

evidence.title: 1954 Cannes Film Festival
evidence.text: This was the last festival with a predominantly French Jury.

evidence.title: A Girl Isn't Allowed to Love
evidence.text: A Girl Isn't Allowed to Love a.k.a. "The Rose Again" (薔薇いくたびか , Bara ikutabika ) is a 1955 Japanese film directed by Teinosuke Kinugasa.
evidence.resolved_title: A Girl Isn't Allowed to Love

evidence.title: Jujiro
evidence.text: Jujiro (十字路 , Jūjiro ) , also known as "Crossroads", "Crossways", "Shadows of the Yoshiwara" or "Slums of Tokyo", is a 1928 silent Japanese film drama directed by Teinosuke Kinugasa.
